lines.text: This skill should be used when the user wants to deconstruct a workflow, break down a business process, capture requirements for an AI workflow, or turn a workflow from their backlog into a clear, testable description of what it must do. It starts from anything already written down, shapes the outcome first (a goal and yes-or-no checks), then how the work gets done, the rules, where a person checks or approves the work, the sources it uses and practice inputs, and saves them as the workflow's requirements for the Design step; small, low-risk workflows get a shorter version. Also use when the user says "continue my workflow" and the workflow needs its requirements: none yet, an unfinished Deconstruct interview, or a big change sent back from Design; and when the user asks to run the deconstruct skill on work that already runs outside the framework (an in-production Workflow node with no workflow folder), to bring it in. This is the Deconstruct step of the AI Workflow Framework.

lines.text: This skill should be used when the user has a workflow's requirements and wants to plan how AI will do the work: which parts are skills or agents, how much the AI decides at each step, where a person checks, what it connects to, and how each part will be checked. It writes a plan the Build step follows, task by task, and asks the user only what only they can decide. Also use when the user says "continue my workflow" and the workflow needs its plan, a plan was stopped partway, or Build sent back a question; and when the user says "change my workflow" to change one that's planned, built or live. This is the Design step of the AI Workflow Framework.

lines.text: This skill should be used when the user has an approved Design Plan and wants to build their AI workflow. It sets up the workflow's place with the user, builds each task in the plan (skills, agents, connections and any schedule), checks each one against what it must do without making any real change, then saves or installs the workflow where it runs and writes a build record that says what was built and what it can access. Also use when the user says "continue my workflow" and the workflow needs building: an approved plan not built yet, a build that stopped partway, misses from a test round for Build to fix, or an approved change to a workflow that's already live. Not for "build my knowledge graph": that is the building-knowledge-graph skill. This is the Build step of the AI Workflow Framework.

lines.text: This skill should be used when the user has built an AI workflow and wants to test it before relying on it, says "test the workflow I built", or wants to re-check a workflow that's already live. It runs the workflow cold on practice inputs, including one real example it hasn't seen, never sends or changes anything real, checks every requirement with the proof, and lets the user decide what to fix or accept; when it's ready, it takes the workflow live and sets when to re-check it. Also use when the user says "continue my workflow" and the workflow is built and waiting for its first test round, a round is in progress or waiting on access, a fix or change has been built and needs testing again, or the workflow is live, whether or not its re-check is due. This is the Test step of the AI Workflow Framework.
